First, we select the identity that contains a ${tan}^{2}⁡x$ term. So we can use the identity 

$$
1+{tan}^{2}⁡x={sec}^{2}⁡x.
$$

Using the above, we compute the given integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{\operatorname{sec}⁡x}{1+{tan}^{2}⁡x}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{\operatorname{sec}⁡x}{{sec}^{2}⁡x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int \frac{1}{\operatorname{sec}⁡x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int \operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x+C\end{aligned}
$$
